reasons: The cited Section 11.3 confirms the gap: it covers survival, run-off use rights and a mutual return-or-destroy of Confidential Information, but contains no data export/return right (no format, no timing, no machine-readable requirement) and no transition assistance obligation, so 'missing' is the correct status for a hosted-service agreement.

Direction is correct for our side: Corio is the customer/licensee and the inserted Section 11.4 places all obligations (assistance, return, deletion, certification) on Commerce One, the hosting licensor.

The insertion tracks the preferred position and model language closely (six months' assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable return within thirty days, deletion plus written certification), and is added as a new paragraph in the termination section without disturbing the existing text \u2014 the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position.

Tailoring is appropriate: it covers Corio's Customers' data and data held in the MarketSite.net Service, and the added survival sentence is necessary because 11.3's survival list would otherwise omit the new clause. Making return/deletion Corio-triggered avoids conflict with the surviving run-off and support obligations in 11.3.
Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the [Playbook] prefix, explains the change and rationale, and offers the 90-day fallback as sanctioned by the rule.
